newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks march ahead on improved liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks march ahead on improved liquidity.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks marched higher on Tuesday on improved liquidity as investors continued deserting the money market where short-term trading rates have been falling steadily in recent months.
The key 57-stock industrial index leapt 41.2 points to break through the 8,000 pyschological barrier -- its second break this year -- to close at 8,010.93.

"Providing the liquidity we are seeing remains as it is, the market is going to continue higher," one broker said, adding the first rains for the season which started at the weekend had also boosted investor sentiment.

Among the day's winners, cement producer Circle rose 30 cents to 700, sugar firm Hippo, pork processor Colcom and packaging group Hunyani each climbed 20 cents to 890, 380 and 340 respectively while discount house DCZ gained 15 cents to 185.

Seed manufacturer and distributor SeedCo at 210, construction firm J and F at 200, transport group Clan at 300, horticulture Ariston at 1,500 and electronics company Apex at 140 all added 10 cents, while several other counters registered five-cent gains.
Cable manufacturer BICAF -- 25 cents down at 325 -- and clothing and furniture group Tedco -- 10 cents lower at 640 -- were the only losers.
Minings were quietly firmer with Wankie colliery rising 15 cents to 395, while Falgold at 135 cents and copper producer Mhangura at 20 cents were both unchanged.
The seven-counter mining index ended 6.59 points up at 1,222.50.
